Yes, the choice to put the options menu behind progression is a little weird, but I just adjusted the sound with the volume mixer, and yes, the lack of an in-game quit button is weird, but alt-f4 works. If this game wasn't as well polished as it is in every other respect, I wouldn't be as willing to overlook these two weird choices, but because the game is so well made in every other respect, I am willing to overlook these choices as quirks. Ultimately, they did not detract from my experience beyond causing me to raise an eyebrow quizzically as I discovered them. Overall, I enjoyed this game thoroughly. Edit: I found out how to fix it on desktop: - Open Control Panel - Go to System & Security - Go to System - Select Advanced system settings - Select Environmental Variables - Create a new System Variable (NOT USER VARIABLE) - Enter the following into the Variable name box: OPENSSL_ia32cap - Enter the following into the Variable value box: ~0x20000000 - Now press OK Thanks to PracticalAd570 on reddit for the fix.

[h1]A haunting, melancholy investigation, putting together fragments of interviews to build a coherent story.[/h1] I just played through this short (~3 hr) mystery and really enjoyed it. It's about trying to make sense of an old investigation that is fragmented in the protagonist's memory - she remembers interviewing many witnesses, and remembers what was said, but doesn't remember who said what, or when. So it turns into a massive jigsaw puzzle where you have to fit ideas together, and assign them to the speakers who make the most sense, in the right order. The mechanics are very simple - it's understanding that is the real challenge. The deeper you go, the more new pieces appear. I found the story very convoluted and difficult to follow at first, which seems to be the intention. Made me want to play it all in one sitting (which I did) so I wouldn't forget anything. The more you fit it together, the more it makes sense. I found it very rewarding. The mood is melancholy and bittersweet - watch the trailer to get a feel for it. It [title] also be said that I really liked the epilogue. Very much worth collecting enough keys to unlock the "true ending". Really sweet, haunting soundtrack too. Just a couple tracks but easily worth an extra 69¢! Worth full price and your time, inexpensive plus 30% off right now for Detective Fest.

Specifically, the game lets you know early that a victory will carve consequences towards the rest of your teammates or your opponents, who may deserve a win more than you. In other words, would your decision-making change if you knew your star player would disappear if you won the game with 7 more games to go this season? And, each game could let your teammates leave purgatory. Ranks as the most underrated game in the last 10 years to me.

I was digging around for a new puzzle game and found this gem. For the price, I highly recommend it. Took me just under 11 hours of casual play to 100%, time may vary depending on experience with these kinds of games and how seriously you go at it. But it's definitely not perfect, as while some of the earlier levels introduce the game's nuances, there aren't enough to keep the game fresh for 150 levels. Some later levels (looking at you S13 and 118) really shine though. The developer also could have used a good playtester or two to help him catch faster solutions, but it's only a little off-putting now and then if that. Oh, and I wish we got more levels with the bow, and fewer shield+glove repeats but alas. Anyway, it's a solid game and if the dev happens to read this hit me up if you ever need someone to help you lower move counts, I might not be of too much help but I'm sure I'll be able to find something.
